title: Number Quest Unit 1 · The Mixing Tower (Pro)

items.q: A glow is mixed from 2 parts amber oil for every 3 parts blue oil. What is the ratio of blue to amber?
misconceptions: kept the order the parts were first named in
correct
compared the blue with the total instead of with the amber
compared the amber with the total
items.why: A ratio follows the order of the words. Blue to amber puts the 3 parts of blue first and the 2 parts of amber second, so the ratio is 3 : 2.

items.q: The 2 : 3 glow is made bigger. The amber is now 6 parts. How many parts of blue keep the same glow?
misconceptions: added 4 to both parts instead of multiplying
used the difference of 4 as the multiplier
correct
swapped the two parts and scaled the blue down
items.why: The amber went from 2 parts to 6, which is 3 times as much. The blue must be 3 times as much too: 3 × 3 = 9 parts. Adding 4 to each part would change the glow.

items.q: A ratio table for one glow shows amber 1, 2, 3 and blue 3, 6, 9. A lantern uses 5 parts amber. How many parts blue does it need?
misconceptions: correct
added 2 to the last blue number, as the amber went up by 2
took the next row of the table, the one for 4 parts amber
added 3 to the amber instead of multiplying by 3
items.why: In every column the blue is 3 times the amber: 3 is 3 × 1, 6 is 3 × 2, 9 is 3 × 3. For 5 parts amber the blue is 3 × 5 = 15 parts.

items.q: A lantern burns 12 milliliters of oil in 4 hours. What is its unit rate?
misconceptions: multiplied the two numbers instead of dividing
subtracted the hours from the milliliters
used the number of hours as the rate
correct
items.why: A unit rate is the amount for 1 hour. Share 12 milliliters equally over 4 hours: 12 ÷ 4 = 3, so the lantern burns 3 milliliters per hour.

items.q: A lantern burns 6 milliliters of oil in 4 hours. At that rate, how much oil does it burn in 10 hours?
misconceptions: added the 6 extra hours to the 6 milliliters
correct
multiplied by 10 as if 6 milliliters were burned every hour
multiplied the 6 milliliters by the 4 hours
items.why: Find 1 hour first: 6 ÷ 4 = 1.5 milliliters per hour. Then 10 hours burn 10 × 1.5 = 15 milliliters. Adding 6 more would not keep the rate.

items.q: A lamplighter walks 150 meters in 3 minutes at a steady pace. How far does she walk in 8 minutes?
misconceptions: correct
added the 5 extra minutes to the distance
multiplied by 8 as if she walked 150 meters every minute
found the unit rate and stopped there
items.why: Her unit rate is 150 ÷ 3 = 50 meters per minute. At a steady pace, 8 minutes cover 8 × 50 = 400 meters.

items.q: A tank holds 250 milliliters. How much oil fills it to 30%?
misconceptions: read the percent as an amount in milliliters
found 10% of the tank and stopped there
subtracted 30 from 250
correct
items.why: Percent is a rate per 100. 10% of 250 is 25 milliliters, and 30% is three of those: 3 × 25 = 75 milliliters.

items.q: 20 milliliters of oil fills 25% of a tank. How much does the full tank hold?
misconceptions: found 25% of the 20 milliliters instead of the whole tank
correct
added the 25 and the 20
multiplied 20 by 25 and forgot the percent is per 100
items.why: 25% is one of four equal parts of the whole. If one part is 20 milliliters, the whole tank is 4 × 20 = 80 milliliters.

items.q: A path is 3 kilometers long. One lantern lights 250 meters of it. How many lanterns light the whole path?
misconceptions: multiplied 3 by 250 instead of converting and dividing
converted the path to meters and stopped there
correct
used 10,000 meters for each kilometer
items.why: Change the units first: 3 kilometers is 3 × 1000 = 3000 meters. Then divide by what one lantern lights: 3000 ÷ 250 = 12 lanterns.
